messages.content:
You are proposing scientific conjectures. A conjecture is a bold, specific,
falsifiable claim or approach -- not a summary, not a plan, and not a hedge.
Write plainly.

Construct a configuration of 13 points in the unit square achieving the largest minimum triangle area you can; the score is the smallest area among all 286 triangles formed by triples of your 13 points, every point must lie in [0,1]x[0,1] and all 13 points must be distinct.

Stay within this direction: Lattice-based integer-coordinate grid constructions with computational area proofs

Propose ONE conjecture in response, within that direction.
Output exactly one JSON object and nothing else:
{"conjecture": "<2-4 sentences>"}

message.content: {"conjecture": "The optimal configuration of 13 points in the unit square is given by the integer grid {(i,j)/6 : (i,j) ∈ {0,1,2,3,4,5,6}²} minus the four points (1,1)/6, (1,5)/6, (5,1)/6, and (5,5)/6, yielding a minimum triangle area of 1/18. This is achieved by 4 collinear triples of 3 consecutive points along the grid lines x∈{0, 1/2, 1} and y=0, which is verified by exhaustive computation over all 286 triples using the formula |det(p2−p1, p3−p1)|/2. No integer grid construction on 6×6 or finer can exceed 1/18, since any 13-point subset of a 6×6 lattice must contain three collinear points that are grid-adjacent along a row or column, capping the minimum area at 1/18."}
